title: Adaptive output heuristics — personal PRD sketch
content:
Context / one-line idea:
A lightweight client+server heuristic that adapts response fidelity per request in order to hit latency/cost targets while preserving perceived quality. Think: automatically choose between micro-replies, compressed recaps, or full generation based on signals (client hint, session priority, token budget, and model confidence).

Why this? (problem statement)
- Customers ask for lower predictable cost without sacrificing UX. Many apps have mixed intents in a single session (fast checks, deep writing, clarifying follow-ups).
- Current knobs (model size, temperature, max_tokens) are blunt and require manual engineering.
- We can reduce token spend and time-to-first-byte by selecting different output shapes instead of single monolithic outputs.

Primary goals (what success looks like)
- 20–40% average token-cost reduction on mixed workloads (measured across internal synthetic mixes) without a >2% drop in downstream task accuracy (when applicable).
- P95 latency improvement for high-priority short intents: target 30% lower.
- Clear developer controls: API flags + per-route dashboard showing fidelity mode distribution and cost delta.

Non-goals
- This is not a replacement for model compression/quantization. It sits above those.
- Not aiming to change core model architectures or training.

High-level proposal
1) Introduce 'fidelity_hint' in requests with optional values: [full, concise, summary-first, micro-reply, auto]. Default = auto.
2) Server-side policy engine maps fidelity_hint + signals -> output strategy. Signals include: recent response length statistics, session token budget, route SLA / priority, model confidence (nucleus entropy proxy), and historical user acceptance (thumbs/up metrics).
3) Output strategies (examples):
   - micro-reply: return a 1–2 sentence answer, then stream an affordance for expanded details.
   - concise: compacted response that aims for 40–60% token reduction via aggressive phrasing and prioritized facts.
   - summary-first: produce a 1–2 sentence summary and optionally continue full context if user asks. Good for long-form completions.
   - full: unchanged, normal generation.
4) Developer controls: per-route defaults, per-request override, opt-in telemetry, opt-out per customer.

User stories / acceptance criteria (rough)
- As a product engineer, I can add fidelity_hint=auto to my route and get cost savings without changing existing prompts. AC: With auto, 30-day cost delta shows reduced tokens tied to the route.
- As an end user, I get quick short answers for quick queries and can expand for more detail. AC: 90% of micro-reply results get an expand click within 10s when expansion was useful (tracked).
- As an SRE, I can set capacity rules such that when capacity is constrained, low-priority routes receive micro-reply fallbacks. AC: under simulated capacity-burst, route fallback happened and error rate remained within SLA.

API sketch (request/response examples)
- Request (JSON): {"input": "How do I optimize embeddings for retrieval?", "fidelity_hint": "auto", "session": {"priority": "low", "token_budget": 800}}
- Response (micro-reply): {"choice": "A compact set of tactics: use smaller embedding dimension for high-throughput retrieval; increase vector store density; quantize embeddings; index granularly. [expand for details]"}

Instrumentation / telemetry
- Per-request logs: fidelity_mode_selected, tokens_out, latency_first_byte, latency_total, expand_clicked (bool), user_feedback (thumbs).
- Dashboard: fidelity distribution per-route, token savings (%), expansion conversion rate, quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

Experimentation plan (MVP -> iterations)
MVP (4 weeks):
- Implement server-side policy with three modes: full / concise / micro-reply.
- Add fidelity_hint in API and per-route default toggle in Console (beta).
- Basic telemetry and A/B test framework for a handful of internal routes.
Measurement: run on synthetic mixed workload (distribution: 40% single-shot Q/A, 40% short clarifications, 20% long-form drafting) and measure token reduction + downstream evals.

Iterate (8–12 weeks):
- Add model confidence signals and simple learn-to-route rules (rule weights learned from offline data).
- Add streaming affordances for expand-first flows.
- Expose per-customer opt-in toggle and cost simulation tool in Console.

Rollout phases
- Internal alpha: product teams + SEs.
- Beta: small set of customers (GTM partner programs) with monitoring and rollback controls.
- GA: public with docs and best-practice guide.

Metrics and SLOs to watch
- Token savings (mean, p90) per route and globally.
- User-perceived quality (evaluation suites + thumbs up). Target <2% task accuracy regression.
- Expansion conversion rate (is concise/micro-reply losing engagement?).
- Latency improvements for selected intents.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: perceived drop in quality for high-precision tasks (legal, medical). Mitigation: route-level allowlist that forces full fidelity, and require customer opt-in for auto on known-sensitive routes.
- Risk: model hallucination increases when compressing content. Mitigation: conservative compression heuristics (preserve named entities, sources) and monitor hallucination signals via evals.
- Risk: developer confusion over new signal. Mitigation: clear Console UX, examples, safety defaults (auto = conservative).

Open questions / TODOs
- How to robustly estimate model "confidence" for generative outputs? (entropy proxies, log-prob mass, contrastive scoring?) Need ML input (cc: Mika).
- UX: what does expand affordance look like in streaming vs non-streaming clients? Ask UX teammates.
- Billing implications: show token-savings vs bill impact in Console preview (finance approval).
- Can we leverage existing KV/prefix caching to make micro-replies faster? (Noah to check caching layers).

Short experiment ideas (very cheap)
- A/B test: concise vs full on internal help-center route (expected many short clarifications). Metric: tokens per session, user follow-up rate.
- Capacity-triggered fallback: simulate high load and measure success of micro-reply fallbacks across low-priority routes.

Next steps (this week)
- Sync with Mika + Noah to validate confidence signals feasibility.
- Prototype server-side policy stub in a feature branch (serving-runtime) and a simple route-level Console toggle.
- Draft short docs for SEs with examples and suggested prompts for concise mode.

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Could pair with "session presets" (e.g., user toggles "economy mode") so preferences survive across requests.
- Consider a hybrid mode: produce short answer + attach a compressed tokenized expansion that client can request and recombine locally to avoid extra model calls. Might be over-engineering.
- Long-term: couple with model selection (tiny->small->base) for each strategy.

Slack threads / references I keep seeing: #model-confidence, #cost-economics, PRD link (above).

Rough timeline estimate: 3 engineers (1 infra, 1 runtime, 1 product eng) + 1 PM + 1 UX for an MVP in ~6 weeks to alpha.

End of scratch — probably messy. Will refine after syncs.
